comments.text_zh: 直到不久之前，所有治愈衰老的尝试都是基于魔法/宗教的。而且这也不像我们“学会了飞行”——仿佛穴居人只要知道正确的翅膀形状和手臂技巧就能做到。它之所以成为可能，只是因为工业与科学知识的积累。显著的寿命延长很可能也将建立在同样的知识积累之上，而不是某种古人本可以提炼出来的雨林青蛙提取物。我能想象我们 1000 年后还没有这项技术的唯一方式，就是某人的核按钮手指发痒。想加速研究？让《The Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant》成为所有学龄儿童的必读/必看：[VIDEO]（这件事可能引发争议，这本身就很有意思。）
comments.text: All attempts to cure aging have been magic/religion-based until very recently. Also it's not like we "learned to fly" as if cavemen could have done it had they only known the right wing shape and arm technique. It was only possible because of an accumulation of industrial and scientific knowledge. Significant life extension will likely be built off the same accumulation of knowledge, not some rainforest frog extract the ancients could have refined. The only way I can imagine we don't have this in 1000 years is if someone's nuke finger gets twitchy. Want to accelerate research? Make "The Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant" required reading/watching for all schoolchildren: [VIDEO] (That this might be controversial is itself interesting.)

Have in mind though that as with any technology it is not good or bad, and if it is possible someone will do it sooner or later. comments.quote_zh: 我一直觉得这是个有趣的话题。更多内容见这里
comments.text_zh: 我一直觉得这是个有趣的话题。更多内容见这里：[VIDEO]。那里提出的论点基本上是，死亡（至少就人类衰老而言）是一种状况，或者如果你愿意，也可以说是一种疾病，和其他疾病一样，只要投入足够资源就可以解决。也许真正的问题是，寿命延长发生在哪个尺度上？如果我们仍然在同一年龄进入成年，然后进入更受限制的老年生活方式，只是通过良好的医疗实践延长老年状态，那是一回事。但如果我们能总体上减缓衰老，从而延长年轻和中年阶段，那完全是另一回事。
comments.text: I've always found this to be an interesting topic. See here for more: [VIDEO] . The argument made there is basically that death (human aging, at any rate) is a sort of condition, or disease, if you will, like any other, that could be solved if we plied it with enough resources. Maybe the real question is where on the scale the extension to life happens? If we keep reaching adulthood, and then elderly, more inhibited lifestyles at the same ages, just prolonging the elderly state via good medical practices, that's one thing. But if we could slow aging in general to extend younger and middle-aged sections of life, that'd be another thing altogether.

comments.text: I have to say I like this somewhat poetic way of writing, especially the sentences with which the author ends paragraphs. Very rich. On a different note, no. Let's fight death. Fuck aging. We can fight it. We don't have to suffer like cattle under it. We can beat it. There are plenty of longevity focused startups and academic research groups, and yet we're not spending nearly enough effort and money on this problem. It affects every human on earth, and the immense benefits of adding even one year of healthy lifespan to 7 billion people make it a moral imperative to act upon. Fighting death should be a multi-national effort that we focus on with all our might, _right now_. You shouldn't have to die. Related: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 现在正是请求对 CGP Grey 关于应该发明永生的立场提出反论的好时机：[VIDEO] 假设有一种技术 X 最终会被发明出来。再假设，按某种对不道德的定义，它是一种极不道德的技术。那么，创造 X 因此就是不道德的吗？注意：约束条件是 X 不可避免。唯一的问题是，谁先创造它。在这种情况下，难道至少不能从多个维度论证，你应该帮助创造它吗？这个论证的极端情形会是：“你对所生活的社会有责任，确保它拥有竞争优势，而不是让某个别的社会拥有。”一种不那么敌意的说法是：“最先发明某项技术的公司，随后可以尝试把伦理强加到这项技术上。”也就是说，如果你发明了某样东西，你就比没发明它的人更容易规定它如何使用。因此，看似矛盾的是，逻辑结论似乎会是：你应该尽可能努力地去发明你所担心的那种不道德技术——希望以后能把损害降到最低。如果某项技术看起来真的无法控制（例如核武器），我用这个来反驳：Bitcoin 是一组理念的一种实现。具体的实现方式本可能非常不同。例如，它本可以是通胀性的，而不是通缩性的。这些精确选择非常重要，因为 Bitcoin 拥有巨大的先发优势
comments.text: This is an excellent time to ask for a counterargument to CGP Grey's stance that immortality should be invented: [VIDEO] Suppose there were a technology X which was going to be invented eventually. Suppose also that it's a highly unethical technology, for some definition of unethical. Is it therefore unethical to create X? Note: The constraint is that X is inevitable . The only question is who creates it first. And in that context, isn't it at least possible to argue from multiple axes that you should help to create it? The limit case of this argument would be "It's your duty to the society you live in to ensure it has the competitive advantage, not some other society." A less-hostile way to phrase that would be "The first company to invent a technology can then try to enforce ethics onto that technology." That is, if you invent something, it's easier to dictate how it's used than if you didn't. Hence, paradoxically as it may seem, the logical conclusion would seem to be that you should work as hard as you can to invent whatever unethical technology you're worried about -- in the hopes that you can minimize the damage later. If it seems like a technology can't really be controlled (e.g. nuclear weapons), I counter with this: Bitcoin was the implementation of a set of ideas. The exact implementation could have been very different. It could have been inflationary rather than deflationary, for example. comments.text_zh: 相关：Fable of the Dragon Tyrant [VIDEO] 提高预期寿命的方法：A. 让孩子活到成年（基本已做到） B. 让成年人不得病/保持健康（部分做到） C. 让老人活到自然死亡（几乎没做到） D. 阻止自然死亡（可能吗？） E. 逆转衰老（可能吗？） 如果自然死亡只是不断地掷体质检定，掷得够久总会掷出大失败，那么也许完成 C 就够了。如果自然死亡是某种细胞倒计时，那么像 D 那样把时间停住也许就足够了。我认为对大多数人来说，他们真正想要的不是以 90 多岁的身体永生，而是能够活在年轻的身体里，这就需要 E。想想我们只完成其中一些、而非全部的情景会很有意思，尤其是 C 和/或 D 可能实现、但 E 不能实现的情况。
comments.text: Related: Fable of the Dragon Tyrant [VIDEO] Ways to improve life expectancy: A. keep children alive till adulthood (mostly done) B. keep adults disease-free/healthy (somewhat done) C. keep old people alive till natural death (little done) D. stop natural death (possible?) E. reverse aging (possible?) If natural death is just rolling constitution checks long enough to get a critical miss, then perhaps it's enough to complete C. If natural death is some sort of cellular countdown, it may suffice to stop the time, as in D. I think for most people, what they really want is not eternal life in a 90+ year-old body, but to be able to live in a young body, which necessitates E. It's interesting to consider scenarios where we accomplish some but not all of these, especially where C and/or D are possible but E is not.

comments.text_zh: 我觉得这是因为人们以为自己不再成长了。我当时在听 Levitt 的 People I (Mostly) Admire，最近一期节目里他在聊进步这件事。每个人都会说过去十年里自己变了，但如果你问他们接下来十年会变成什么样，他们觉得自己还是老样子。可其实有很多洞见是我们常常忽略的。我觉得同样地，人们也忽略了政治和文化上的进步。把缺乏进步归咎于守旧派很容易。但回头看历史，我们的前进速度比那快得多。一个很好的例子是同性婚姻的合法化。Pee [0] 追踪了人们对它的支持度，很明显态度的转变速度比老一辈人死去的速度更快。另外我觉得问题的一部分在于，我们都习惯了那个恶龙暴君[1]，于是就接受了命运。[0] [LINK] [1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I think it's because people think they stop growing. I was listening to Levitt's People I (Mostly) Admire and on a recent show he was talking about progress. How everyone will say in the last 10 years they've changed but if you ask them what they'll be in the next 10 years they think they'll be the same. But there's a lot of insight we often ignore. I think similarly people ignore political and cultural progress. It's easy to blame the lack of progress on the old guard. But if we look at history we go much faster than that. One great example of this is the legalization of gay marriage. Pee [0] tracks support of it and it's clear that attitude is changing faster than the old people dying. Also I think part of the problem is we've all gotten used to the Dragon Tyrant[1] that we accept our fate. [0] [LINK] [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: mjevans
comments.why_zh: 用龙的隐喻指代战胜死亡
comments.quote_zh: 我希望科技能在我、在我们所有人走到终点之前拯救我、拯救我们大家
comments.text_zh: 我希望科技能在我、在我们所有人走到终点之前拯救我、拯救我们大家……但在我们击败那条“龙”之前还得等着。（[VIDEO] CGP Grey - Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant）有一个临界点：如果那时我还剩下点什么——而碰上痴呆症或其他破坏大脑的疾病／损伤，可能什么都不剩了——那就只是在延长痛苦。目前的医疗表格并没有真正清楚说明什么时候算到了那条曲线上的拐点；它们假定的是全都要或全都不要，至少从我父母身上最近一次遇到这情况时我看到的是这样。我知道我不愿意被当成实际上的一具植物人那样留着，靠一个“端口”往我的胃肠道里灌液体，对人生几乎什么都记不住，还要被拖上好些年的痛苦。那就是你说的那种剥削的部分。你说的那种尊严的缺失。把病人变成一个利润中心，而不是为他们的最大利益着想。也许有一天，我们不必再面对如今大家都面临的这种没有真正选择权的处境。在那之前，也许甚至在那之后，给人们选择的自由。也给他们真正的选择，比如心理咨询，以及帮助他们作为受重视的、有生产力的社会成员融入社会。
comments.text: I hope technology can save me, save us all, before the end comes... but until we defeat that 'dragon'. ( [VIDEO] CGP Gray - Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant ) There's a point where if there is any of me left, which with dementia and other brain destroying disease / injury might not even be anything, it's just prolonging the suffering. Current medical forms don't really give a clear indication about when the infection point on that curve is reached; they assume all in or all out, at least from what I saw when it last came up among my parent's experiences. I know I wouldn't want to be kept around as effectively a vegetable, surviving on a 'port' forcing fluids into my GI tract, barely remembering anything about life and being strung out on many years of suffering. That's the exploitative part you mention. The lack of dignity you mention. The turning a patient into a profit center rather than looking out for their best interests. Maybe someday that won't be the lack of real choice we all currently face. Until then, and maybe even after, give people the freedom to choose. Also give them real choices, like counseling and assistance fitting into society as a productive member who's valued.
